You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Input contains two binary-like panels separated by a solid line (orientation may vary), with zero as background and nonzero cells representing filled locations. Compare panels at corresponding coordinates and output their intersection: place color 2 wherever both panel cells are nonzero; all other output cells are 0. Output dimensions equal one panel. Demonstrations: stacked 12x27 panels (upper color-0 sparse pattern on color-3 field; lower color-8 pattern on zero field) produced color-2 at positions where both panels were nonzero, i.e. upper 3 and lower 8. Side-by-side 13x9 panels (colors 4 and 5, zero background) confirmed intersection. Vertical-separator demo with non-overlapping nonzero positions yielded all-zero output. Test with 5x9 panels colors 1 and 9 solved by aligned overlap, output color 2. Important: zero is the empty/background value even where another panel has a nonzero background-like field; the correct rule is nonzero/nonzero intersection, not subtraction or background masking. Initial failed attempt used lower-panel nonzeros where upper panel was zero; do not repeat.', path='continual_arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:27:48.100586+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T10:27:48.100598+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='continual_arc_task_4831a9db_mark_equal_cells_across_divided_panels', kind='memory', title='Continual-ARC task-4831a9db: mark equal cells across divided panels', content='Task-4831a9db solved. Input consists of two same-sized binary panels separated by a solid line (separator may be vertical or horizontal). Compare corresponding cells. Output has panel dimensions. Use the shared/background color as output background and color 3 to mark positions where the two panel cells are equal. Demonstrations: vertical panels left colors 8/4 and right 4/7, separator 2; output background 4 with 3 at equal cells. Horizontal panels top 4/5 and bottom 4/2, separator 9; output background 4 and 3 at positions where both cells are 4. Test had vertical panels of 0/6 and 0/9 separated by 8; output 0 background with 3 where both panels were 0. Practical rule: strip the separator, align panels cellwise, produce color 3 on equality and the shared color (the common color between the panels) elsewhere.', path='continual_arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:02:45.633233+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T10:02:45.633246+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='continual_arc_task_c5508678_crop_and_decode_colored_grid_intersections', kind='memory', title='Continual-ARC task-c5508678: crop and decode colored grid intersections', content='Task-c5508678 solved. Input is a grid of uniform base-color rectangular cells separated by a background-colored grid. At intersections of horizontal and vertical separator lines, some grid-line pixels are recolored; the output is the base-cell-color grid decoded from these intersection markers. Identify separator-line coordinates (periodic horizontal/vertical stripes) and the special/non-background marker values at their crossings. Crop to the bounding range of marked crossing coordinates: only consecutive separator coordinates between the outermost marked intersections contribute output rows/columns. For each adjacent pair of horizontal lines and adjacent pair of vertical lines in this cropped range, inspect the four corner intersection colors. If all four are the same color and that color differs from the separator/background color, output that marker color; otherwise output the uniform interior/base-cell color. Demo5 showed cropping matters: an unmarked top row/column region must be excluded. Test task-c5508678: base interior 9, separator background 2; marked horizontal rows 0,8,16 and active vertical crossings cols 8,11,14,17,20,23; decoded output [[5,9,9,9,3],[9,9,5,9,9]]. Key lesson from wrong attempts: do not include unmarked outer grid cells; crop marker rows/columns first, and never emit separator background as a decoded cell.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:00:43.565875+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T10:00:43.565888+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='continual_arc_task_1ad201d5_mark_compartments_with_exactly_two_dots', kind='memory', title='Continual-ARC task-1ad201d5: mark panels with at least two markers', content='Task-1ad201d5: Full separator rows/columns partition the grid into panels. Identify panel background B and sparse marker color M. Emit a compact grid with one cell per panel, preserving row/column order: output 1 if the panel contains at least two M cells; if it contains zero or one marker, output its original background B. Ignore separator lines. Confirmed across panels of varying sizes (2 demos of 5x4 panels, one of 3x3 panels) and a solved test. Crucial: three markers also output 1; the criterion is >=2, not exactly 2.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T08:54:09.185412+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T09:16:37.469400+00:00', version=2), HarnessEntry(id='continual_arc_decode_colored_marks_on_tiled_grid_intersections', kind='memory', title='Continual-ARC: decode colored marks on tiled grid intersections', content='Solved task-c5508678. Reusable rule: A large grid has a repeated tile texture (the output background color) and a regular lattice of separator/intersection points. Identify the lattice spacing and sample the separator value at its intersection points. Ignore points holding the ordinary separator color; special colors are marks. Crop the lattice to the bounding rows/columns containing any special marks, then consider each adjacent 2×2 block of lattice points. The corresponding output cell is the repeated tile/background color unless all four corner samples are the same special color, in which case output that color. Thus each output cell represents a uniform colored 2×2 corner square; isolated/partial marks do not transfer. Output dimensions are (number of active lattice rows−1) × (number of active lattice columns−1); do not include unmarked outer lattice rows/columns. Verified on demos: task-c5508678 output background is the tile interior (2 in demo1, 9 in demo2, 0 in demo3); special corner squares copy their mark color. For its test, active lattice was rows r3..r18 and columns c2..c26, producing 5×4 output. One initial attempt was wrong because it included unmarked outer lattice rows; trim to active marked bounds.', path='continual_arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T09:53:12.457411+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T09:53:12.457422+00:00', version=1)]
